name: Community pharmacy poisons register and pharmacist attendance/engagement records (e-register with 5-year retention)
buyer: Independent community pharmacies and small chains holding Type A poisons licences
trigger: Poisons Act 1952 s23 Poisons Book and s24 Prescription Book; Poisons Regulations amendment (Parliament paper ST.164/2025) adds Form D pharmacist engagement record and Form E daily attendance, registers kept 5 years, offence fine up to RM5,000 or 2 years; Poisons Act amended 2022 (digital records allowed) and 2025 (federal, KKM Pharmacy Enforcement Division).
existing: Competitor search (buku racun digital / poison book software) found no named product; generic pharmacy POS systems probably record sales but their poison-book compliance is unchecked.
unchecked: Whether the amendment is in force and its date; whether POS vendors already print the statutory forms; enforcement frequency; number of independent pharmacies (data.gov.my list exists but not opened); whether KKM accepts vendor e-registers. K14 (price marking) is a different duty and was rejected for a stay.

first_check.duty: Poisons Regulations 1952 reg 26, replaced by P.U.(A) 155/2025: retail Poisons Book (Form B), Prescription Book (Form C) and wholesale book (Form A). New reg 26A requires the licensed pharmacist to keep a record of each registered pharmacist's engagement/employment and daily attendance (under Act s16(4A)). Records are kept for every sale, so the duty is daily. Not verified: commencement date, Form D/E naming, 5-year retention, penalty amount. The parliamentary PDF was binary and could not be read. The 2022 Act amendment raised penalties (up to RM50,000 / 5 years per DKSH). A UKM thesis abstract says the 2022 amendment allowed fully digital pharmacy records, but I did not open the thesis (503).
first_check.market: About 5,271 community pharmacies as of 4 June 2022, per pharmarise.com.my (unverified and internally inconsistent; it also cites 3,835). The MOH FAQ points to a state-by-state statistics table that I did not open. The MOH my.pharma licence list (2025) was not opened.
first_check.competitor: No named Malaysian software advertising Poisons Book, Prescription Book or reg 26A attendance compliance was found in English or Malay searches. Generic pharmacy POS systems exist (Faris Software, cited in a UTHM paper; legacy GS Vision Pharmacy Manager), but whether they print the statutory forms was not checked. MOH systems (PhIS, MyUBAT) are for public facilities, not private community pharmacies. Absence is not proven: these are search gaps.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Peraturan-Peraturan Racun (Pindaan) 2025, P.U.(A) 155/2025 (ST.164/2025), replaces reg 26: Poisons Book on Form B, Prescription Book on Form C, wholesale book on Form A. It adds reg 26A, a record of each registered pharmacist's engagement and daily attendance. I could not confirm the commencement date, the Form D/E labels, the 5-year retention, the RM5,000 penalty or e-register acceptance, because the PDF would not parse. I found no Malaysian product advertising poison-book compliance. That is weak evidence, since local pharmacy POS systems (e.g. Faris, GS Vision) were not checked. Market is about 3,800-5,300 community pharmacies (unverified 2022 figure). Record-keeping is the most common inspection failure. But POS bundling is a likely risk and willingness to pay is modest, so the score stays at 4.

challenge_check.killer: None found. No product, state tool or exemption was identified. Not settled: the commencement date of P.U.(A) 155/2025, whether local pharmacy POS vendors already print Forms B and C (not advertised online), and whether KKM accepts electronic registers.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing killed it. In English and Malay searches, no Malaysian vendor, MOH e-service or association tool advertises Form B Poisons Book, Form C Prescription Book or reg 26A/Form D/E pharmacist attendance records. The duty is real: Poisons (Amendment) Regulations 2025, P.U.(A) 155, made on 26 March 2025, require these records and 5-year retention. I could not read the commencement date because the PDF would not extract. The Sarawak compliance study says recording of supplies is the most-breached provision. Several things hold the score at 4. A 2018 Malay Mail report said the books are rarely checked. Big chains (Caring, Alpro, Big, Watsons/Guardian) probably have in-house systems. Pharmacy POS vendors could easily add the module. And whether KKM accepts e-registers is still unconfirmed.
